data.narrative:
TAE Technologies is a Series G frontier-energy company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The valuation exercise draws from a Climate & Energy comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lilium, LNZA), though narrow-filter peer matching—same stage, adjacent stage, and similar valuation tier—yielded insufficient datapoints (0, 1, and 0 respectively) to support a robust peer-median method.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable triangulation method, applies a 1.25x step-up multiplier to the $1.3B total raised as a proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $1.6B. This reflects typical Series G-to-subsequent-stage value creation observed in comparable financings. The method is grounded in historical progression patterns but lacks company-specific unit economics or revenue/margin data to adjust the multiplier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $1.9B, with a median point of $1.6B. Material uncertainties include the absence of crystallized financial performance metrics, the nascent state of peer comparables at this stage and sector confluence, and limited visibility into capital efficiency relative to the $1.3B deployed to date. A more refined valuation would require disclosure of revenue, burn rate, and technology validation milestones.
